questions.q: What keyword begins a function definition in Python?
questions.explain: def is the keyword used to define a function.

questions.q: What does a function return if it has no explicit return statement?
questions.explain: A function without an explicit return implicitly returns None.

options: A triple-quoted string right under a function's def line, documenting what it does
A required return value for every function
A special type of comment that only works in loops
questions.explain: A docstring documents a function's purpose and can be read programmatically by tools.

questions.q: Why turn repeated validation logic into a function instead of copy-pasting it in each place it's needed?
options: A fix only needs to be made once, since the logic exists in a single named place instead of multiple copies
Functions run faster than any inline code
Python requires all if statements to live inside functions
There is no real benefit either way
questions.explain: Copy-pasted logic can drift out of sync; a single function avoids that problem entirely.

questions.q: In def calculate_line_total(quantity, unit_price), what are quantity and unit_price called?
options: Arguments — only used when calling the function
Parameters — the named inputs the function expects
questions.explain: Parameters are the named inputs listed in a function's definition; arguments are the actual values passed when calling it.
